notes.title: Game Cancelled Indefinitely
notes.notes:
Hello everyone.

This is a hard one for me, so I'm just going to cut to the chase.


I'm cancelling "Spectre's Library" until further notice.


There are several reasons for this, but the main reason I'm doing this is I've lost inspiration to work on it. I've come up with a plan for the next several games I'm going to make and I've thought a LOT about the overall story I'm going to tell. While "Spectre's Library" was originally on that list of future games, it isn't now. The game just... doesn't fit right with the rest of them, and I don't like that. HOWEVER- that doesn't necessarily mean that it's gone forever. We may come back to it at some point, but because of how everything is going, I'm not sure if that'll happen. 

Like I said, there's a lot of reasons for me cancelling it, but I'll go through some of the other major ones:
[b]-It's not enticing, ESPECIALLY the demo.[/b] At the time that I made the demo, I thought that it was perfect just the way it was and that it'd hook people. Looking back, that's completely false. The only thing that seems really interesting is the Goners, and they weren't even main characters!
[b]-It's boring and confusing.[/b] The demo is not a game, it's a poorly designed fetch-quest that leads into ANOTHER poorly designed fetch-quest. There's barely any information given on who you're playing as or why they're there or what the hell is going on, and I've seen people wander the map looking for answers and/or quit out of boredom or rage. I don't think that's fair to anyone to have to go through that. On top of that, seeing people quit out of boredom, confusion, or rage is incredibly demotivating. ESPECIALLY if I agree with them.
[b]-I just don't like it anymore.[/b] There isn't a big explanation for this, I've just thought about it a lot and after seeing what people think, I don't really like it anymore and I wish I had done things with this game differently.

I really wish that I could finish this game, but I just have no ambition to anymore. I'll probably reuse the ideas I had for it elsewhere, but they won't be connected to this game at all.
I'm so sorry for anyone that happened to be interested in seeing the full game. We tried our best, but we just didn't win this one, and the best thing to do would be to put it out of its and everyone else's misery. Like I said, we might come back to it, but with everything going on chances are slim.

But, with this knowledge in hand, I will work hard to make sure that my future games are put together well and do not suffer the same fate as this one. I hope everyone will stick around to see them!

Anyway, that's it from me.
I hope everyone is having a great day!!
We'll see you next time!
-Matt

notes.title: May 2023 Update!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

I know I haven't done an update on this game for a little while, and that's mainly because I've been working on another smaller game. I am almost done with it though, and I'm hoping by the end of June I can release it and finally get back into production on "Spectre's Library". I'm still excited to get it done, and I think working on my other project has definitely helped me form a more solid base and story for this game as well.

But that's not the main reason I'm making this update post. I'm actually making this post because I went back into the demo and fixed a few bugs that I noticed were there. There wasn't anything major, but I figured I shouldn't leave it in an unfixed state. There were a few main things I fixed, including making one of the puzzles' hints more understandable, and re-exporting the demo to include the RTP assets so the game can function properly. (I had to do this with the Steam version of the demo when I initially released it, but I didn't think to go back and do this with the GameJolt/Itch.io versions. Oops.) 

As well as fix these bugs, I also renamed the project to "Spectre's Library (DEMO)". I decided that this demo will be the only demo for the game, and there won't be one for the other chapters. This would save a bunch of time, as well as leave the future chapters more of a surprise to players, which I think I like better.

Anyway, I'll wrap this up. I'm very excited for everyone to see the full chapter, and the game as a whole. I know I haven't worked on it in a long time, and that's okay. I was never pressuring myself to get this or any of my current/future projects done in a fast timeframe. I've learned that if I try to pressure myself into getting my games done, the final product suffers a lot because of it, and I won't be satisfied with how it came out. I just hope that you guys can be patient for me to get this done. It will be done, I promise! It just takes time.

If you'd like to check out the demo, you can here:
https://matt-mcgreevy.itch.io/spectres-library-chapter-i-demo
https://gamejolt.com/games/spectreslibrarych1demo/770279

I also stream every week! If you'd like to see my shenanigans, feel free to check me out below:
https://www.youtube.com/@matt_mcgreevy

I hope everyone is doing well, and I hope everyone has a great day today!
I'll see YOU... next time!
-Matt

notes.title: February 2023 Update!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

Spoiler alert, this update doesn't have a lot of details about Spectre's Library, as I have been working on something different for most of this month. That's not to say what I've been working on is bad, it's definitely going to be fun, there just hasn't been much going on with Spectre's Library. What new project have I been working on, you ask? Let me show you!

Shortly after I posted the previous update, I completely lost the motivation to work on Spectre's Library. I did some tweaks to the transition to Rose's story, and I changed part of the beginning of the game, and I feel much better about those parts. It's not a lot, but it's progress, and I'm satisfied with that. I have a few small things that I plan on adding to the game, which I might do sometime soon, but as of now I'm not really motivated to work on the game. Part of it could be from the fact that Rose's story isn't finished, and that the first part of the story is still in a vague layout state. I've done a bunch of maps where the story takes place, but I haven't done anything else yet. I've kinda been waiting on my sister to keep working on the story as well, she's still in school and works on this when she has a chance to. I'm also helping her lay everything out, and our schedules don't always line up. Now, this doesn't surprise me. I know that this game will take time to make, and I haven't been pressuring myself to work on it all the time and get it done in a certain timeframe. I knew that I would probably suffer a little bit of burnout on the game eventually, like I am now, but I'm still inspired and excited to make the game, no matter how long it takes. I just hope that you guys understand that, and are patient and willing to wait until it's ready. I promise you it will be worth the wait. But, if you're not willing to wait and are impatient, I might have something for you very soon...

In my period of unmotivation for Spectre's Library, I got inspired to make a short puzzle game. I've had the basic idea for it for a while, it actually used to be something WAY bigger and different, but I think a short little game would work out well for it too. I'm not going to say its name (yet), but I will hopefully be finishing it up soon. The basic idea is that it would feature 10 puzzle rooms, and that it takes place in the same universe as Spectre's Library. I kinda wanted to build the world around Spectre's Library without having to make people wait for the game to be released. It's a separate story, but a fun one nonetheless. I'm excited to get this out to people, and I think that people will really like it.

As of writing this, I have made 7 of the 10 puzzles, and I've done a little bit of the hidden stuff. I've been mainly focusing on the puzzles, as they're the most fun part to work on. A bit tedious, but fun. I also plan on using some of the puzzles as a base for puzzles in Spectre's Library, so there's that purpose for this little game as well. I'm hoping to have this out for everyone to play by mid-March, if not sooner. Just a warning, it's not going to be free! I plan on releasing it for a dollar, not too much but still a decent price. I don't really like charging people a lot of money for my games, but I'd still want to make a little bit of money too, so...

Anyway, I'm gonna wrap this up. I'm sorry there isn't a lot of Spectre's Library stuff, maybe by the end of March I'll have gained the motivation to work on it again. We'll see. I am excited for people to play the little puzzle game, though!

If you'd like to check out the demo for Spectre's Library, you can here: 
https://matt-mcgreevy.itch.io/spectres-library-chapter-i-demo
https://gamejolt.com/games/spectreslibrarych1demo/770279

I also stream a video game every week, and I occasionally talk about Spectre's Library! If you'd like to see my streaming shenanigans, feel free to below:
https://www.youtube.com/@matt_mcgreevy

I hope everyone is doing well, and I hope everyone has a great day today!
I'll see you all next month!
-Matt

notes.title: January 2023 Update!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

This month has been pretty busy for me, mainly with personal stuff and work. I had a stretch of like a week or two where I was unmotivated, but I'm feeling better now. It hasn't been super eventful in terms of the game, but that doesn't mean I haven't been working on it! What have I been up to, you ask? Let me tell you!

First, I tackled the beginning of the game, which takes place before where the demo starts. I already had an image of how I wanted the introduction to go, so it didn't take super long to do. It went through a couple iterations, but I settled with a version that I liked. It might go through some changes, but they'll likely be small.

Next, I went through all of what I had and implemented the voice acting system. I did have my siblings record some voice clips for the first part of the chapter, but I haven't gone through them and edited them yet. I don't plan on editing them yet, but I did want to have the system ready so I can just put in the final recordings without having to worry about too much. It wasn't terribly difficult to implement, but it was a little tedious.

At this point, I started to feel unmotivated to work on the game. I felt this way for about a week/week and a half. As the motivation and inspiration slowly made it's way back, I started working on maps/level design for Rose's story. I had already started this process before I released the demo; I had made the house where the story starts/takes place.
Then, most recently, I drafted/made the transition to the story, and the story's introduction. It was a lot of audio work, surprisingly, and I pretty much made it on the fly without any plan. This isn't the first time this has happened, sometimes I'll just come up with an idea and it'll come out good. This is one of those times; the intro to the story came out very good. I'll probably make some adjustments later, but for now I'm satisfied.

Anyway, I'm gonna wrap this up. I'm very excited for everyone to see this chapter, and the game as a whole. I'll keep working on it in the background, hopefully next month I'll have a more eventful description of everything that happened.

If you'd like to check out the demo, you can here:
https://matt-mcgreevy.itch.io/spectres-library-chapter-i-demo
https://gamejolt.com/games/spectreslibrarych1demo/770279

I also stream a video game every week, and I occasionally talk about Spectre's Library! If you'd like to see my streaming shenanigans, feel free to below:
https://www.youtube.com/@matt_mcgreevy

I hope everyone is doing well, and I hope everyone has a great day today!
I'll see you all next month!
-Matt
